label: copy-phase input r (fed-back r) in long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never in the original phase or on <DEL>), and only when the input repeats a token that appeared earlier. Its main trigger is the fed-back token r: copy-phase steps with input r hold 71% of activation mass, and all the strongest activations are r at original position 2 being fed back at step L+3 in L=9 sequences. Activity grows with sequence length: L=9 holds 67% of mass, L<=5 essentially never fires, and recall_idx 0-1 almost never fires. The predicate (copy phase, input r, L>=7, recall_idx>=2) reaches dev F1 0.54 and mass recall 0.70. It misses a long tail of weak activations on other fed-back tokens (f, t, 3, y, x, ...), which hold about 30% of mass. It also has false positives on r in shorter or later-position contexts.
